title: Cost every path against the time window
statement: Cost every path through an adaptive lesson against its accepted time window before building, and when shedding optional parts can't fit a path, change the scheme, not the protected parts.
example: One design's ~900-word lesson with a full model runs to 31:00 against a 29-minute ceiling and cannot be shed back under it.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design checks every time in it against an accepted 22 to 29 minute window (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 2). One path, a ~900-word text with a full model, runs to 31:00 and cannot be shed back under 29, because there is nothing left to shed (lines 108-110 and 453). The design treats the remedy, shorter texts in the back third of the year or a split lesson, as a scheme decision rather than a lesson-design one, and never trades the read-aloud, the comprehension checks, the taught word, the modelled write-up or the independent write (lines 111, 453 and 454).
